prompt: A blueprint shows a scaled-down version of a real bridge truss, so the two figures are similar. Which statement is true about similar figures?

choices.label: Corresponding angles are congruent and corresponding sides are proportional
Corresponding angles are proportional and corresponding sides are congruent
Both corresponding angles and corresponding sides are congruent
Corresponding sides are proportional, but the angles can be anything

hint: Scaling a drawing changes lengths but never tilts the corners.

hints.text: Scaling a drawing changes lengths but never tilts the corners.
Angles stay exactly the same size; sides all shrink by the same ratio.
Angles congruent, sides proportional — choice A.

explanation: Similar figures have the same shape but not necessarily the same size.
Same shape means every pair of corresponding angles is congruent — angles do not scale.
Different size means every pair of corresponding sides is in the same ratio, the scale factor. Choice C describes congruent figures, a special case where the scale factor is 1.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think of a photocopier
steps: Copy a drawing at 50% and every length halves.
But a right angle stays a right angle — no angle is ever "halved" by the copier. That is the whole idea of similarity.
